entries.title: Micah 5:1
segments: Now gather thyself; Zion is exhorted to prepare for times of trouble.  Though God will grant her a final victory over all her foes, he will, in the meantime, chastise her for her sins,

. 
 
  Daughter of troops; that is, mistress of troops.  Zion is addressed under the figure of a military city. 
 
  He hath laid; the enemy, to whom there is reference,

. 
 
  The judge of Israel; the chief ruler, who represents the whole people.

entries.title: Micah 5:2
segments: Beth-lehem Ephratah; Ephratah, or Ephrath, was the ancient name of Beth-lehem,

, a small village five or six miles south of Jerusalem. 
 
  Thousands; that is, families, or divisions of tribes; probably so called from the average number of men belonging to them.  See

, etc. 
 
  Shall he come forth; the Messiah,

.  The quotation in Matthew gives the first part of this verse, with free variations not affecting its general meaning. 
 
  Whose goings forth--from everlasting; these words assert the eternity of the Messiah.  The opening words of John's gospel are the best commentary on them. 
 
The Saviour of the world had his birth in a feeble village, and he was brought up in a despised town of Galilee.  Thus God, in the very beginning of the gospel, taught his church to rely not on worldly rank and splendor, but on the power of his Spirit.

entries.title: Micah 5:3
segments: Therefore; in accordance with God's purpose, intimated in

. 
 
  Give them up; leave them, that is, the covenant people, in a depressed condition. 
 
  She which travaileth; see

. 
 
  The remnant of his brethren; the scattered remnant of the Messiah's people.  For the meaning of these words, see

. 
 
God prepares his church for the coming of Christ by a long period of humiliation; and then it was only the pride the remnant of humble Israelites that received him.  Through pride the Jews as a nation rejected him, and thus "the kingdom of God" passed from them to the Gentiles.

entries.title: Micah 5:4
segments:
He shall stand; the Messiah. 
 
  They shall abide; his people shall abide safely under his rule. 
 
vv 4-9. 
 
In the gift of his Son Jesus Christ, God has given his people the highest possible pledge of help in all their troubles, and victory in all their conflicts with the wicked.  Since to him is given "all power in heaven in earth," he must, "be great unto the ends of the earth," and all his enemies "be cut off" before him.

entries.title: Micah 5:5
segments:
And this man--then shall we raise; a preferable pointing of this verse is the following: "And this man shall be the peace.  When the Assyrian shall come into our land, and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise," etc. 
 
  The peace; before his advent the pledge of peace, and the bestower of it afterwards. 
 
  The Assyrian; the Assyrian is here the representative of Zion's enemies in all coming ages. 
 
  Seven--eight; a Hebrew mode of expressing fulness.
, and note on

. 
 
  Principal men; literally, "anointed of men."  These, with the shepherds, represent the helpers whom God raises up for Zion.

entries.title: Micah 5:6
segments: The land of Nimrod; another name for Assyria.

entries.title: Micah 5:7
segments:
As a dew from the Lord; these words describe the benign influence of the gospel as carried by the Jews among the Gentiles. 
 
  That tarrieth not for man; that springs up by the divine blessing without man's help.  For the idea, compare

entries.title: Micah 5:8
segments: Shall be--as a lion; that is, shall overcome and destroy all the enemies of Zion.

entries.title: Micah 5:10
segments: In that day; the day of chastisement already described, which has for its object the purification of Zion, and ends in her enlargement and the destruction of all her foes.  The prophet then enumerates the vain confidences of the people, which shall be destroyed by God's judgments.  Compare the very similar passage,

. 
 
vv 10-15. 
 
From age to age, Christ sits among his people "as a refiner and purifer of silver."  He is continually cleansing the hearts of the truly pious from sin, and separating from among them hypocrites and unbelievers. In advances in strength also; and when her people shall be "all righteous," they shall inherit the earth for ever.
